Commentary.Commentary: So, Zimbabwe need a revised target of 342 in 43 overs (DLS method) from their allotted 43-overs. They have a huge mountain to scale if they are to even get close to this humongous target. Bangladesh are firmly in the driver's seat and are well and truly the favorites to inflict a whitewash. Do we have a big upset in store? Join us in a short while for Zimbabwe's reply.

It was a nightmare day for Zimbabwe bowlers. Everyone was taken to the cleaners and had a day to forget as they were demolished and destroyed by the pair of Liton and Tamim. The decision to bowl first back fired pretty badly for the hosts and they were put to the sword. Only Carl Mumba had some parity as he picked up all the three wickets that fell at the latter stage of the innings but apart from that there was hardly any positives for the touring side.

After being put into bat, the centurions from first and second ODI started off brilliantly and decided to put on a show for people to remember for the rest of their life. They took on the Zimbabwe bowler's and stitched the highest ever partnership for Bangladesh. They were accelerating before rain played spoilsport and reduced the game by 7 overs. After the actual rain went away, it started raining sixes as both the openers went berserk. Liton broke the record for highest score for Bangladesh. He though rode his luck in his epic innings as he was LBW in front of the stumps but Sean Williams did not go upstairs after being turned down. The fielders also helped him by putting down a couple of chances. Tamim too played a sublime knock and centuries from both the openers has taken the hosts to a massive score of 322. Also, remember extra runs will be added on top of it courtesy, DLS method.
What a batting performance from Liton Das and Tamim Iqbal. Sean Williams will be regretting his decision to bowl first because what his bowlers saw was absolute carnage, especially from the former.

NO BALL! It looked touch and go and the umpires have decided to give the batter the benefit of the doubt. Lady luck is shinning brightly on Liton Das and Bangladesh. He half plays his pull shot and it goes high in the air but straight to short fine leg. The fielder there takes the catch but Liton is not going anywhere. He is asking the question and so is Tamim. Both the on-field umpire have a word and take it upstairs. Replays roll in and it is a very tough call. The T.V. umpire though gives the benefit of the doubt to Liton Das and signals it as No Ball. Free Hit to follow.
The catch has been referred upstairs. The umpires are checking for a waist height no ball. Replays roll in and it looks fine. Ohh wait the third umpire thinks otherwise and signals a no ball.

In the air and dropped short. Drama straightaway after resumption. Full ball outside off, Liton comes down the track and swings his bat. The ball falls in front of third man. The fielder from third man runs to his left and across. He dives in front but the ball falls short. The batters take a single. Liton is asking the umpire whether it is a no ball or not as the tourists had 5 fielders outside the circle.

Looks like there is a confusion. Zimbabwe might have had more than 4 fielders outside the circle. Liton is asking the question. Both the umpires are having a word and it looks like they have given the benefit of the doubt to Sean Williams and co.

After a lengthy delay due to rain, we are back! Bangladesh openers, Tamim Iqbal and Liton Das walk out to resume their record stand. Donald Tiripano to finish off his over. Liton to face the first ball post rain.

UPDATE 1825 local (1225 GMT) - Yippie!!! Our prayers have been heard and the rain has stopped, the inspection is done. It will now be a 43-over game and Zimbabwe will have a revised target. The play will resume at 1845 local.

UPDATE 1801 local (1201 GMT) - Good news! The rain has stopped and the covers are coming off. That will be music to the ears of all the cricketing fans. Looking at the drainage system in this part of the world, we should be in for a start very quickly if the rain does not return. There will be an inspection at 1815 local.
UPDATE 1724 local (1124 GMT) - Wish we could give you some good news but unfortunately that is not the case. The rain continues to kill the buzz and we have started to lose overs as well.
UPDATE 1652 local (1052 GMT) - Ugh! Sorry to be the bad news bearer as the hope has been laughed upon by the rain gods and they have opened their gates for the shower again.
Update 1640 local (1040 GMT) - Further good news. The outer covers are coming off and it is getting brighter. Let us pray that it stays this way and we resume ASAP!
Update 1628 local (1028 GMT) - Good news! The rain has stopped and with the drainage here, we should resume pretty quickly.

Just the thing we did not want! The covers are on now and the players are going off. Zimbabwe will be happy with it as they have been on the receiving end so far and will welcome this break. Bangladesh are going on nicely and will want to be back again. Let us hope that it is just a passing shower.

We are all set to begin. The Zimbabwe players are out in the middle. Tamim Iqbal and Liton Das will open the batting for Bangladesh. Carl Mumba will start the proceedings for Zimbabwe.

Pitch report - Tino Mawoyo says that it is a good wicket to bat on. Adds that there is tinge of green on this wicket. States that the ball might spin later on in the game. Further says that the team batting first need to score at least 280.

Mashrafe Mortaza, the Bangladesh skipper, says that the wicket gets better but it is important that we bat first and bat well. On the bowling, Mortaza tells they don't have to think too much about it and tells they just need to execute their plans. Informs there are 4 changes as Shafiul Islam and Al-Amin Hossain are not playing. Afif is making his ODI debut and Mushfiqur is missing out. Tells the important thing is to win the game and execute their plans well.

Sean Williams, the Zimbabwe skipper, says that he would like Mortaza for his outstanding career. Adds that they would like to bowl first and restrict them to a low score. Says that they are looking for 100s from their batsman. Adds that Chamu is struggling with an injury and is hopeful that he is ready for the T20s.

Zimbabwe (Unchanged Playing XI) - Tinashe Kamunhukamwe, Regis Chakabva, Sean Williams (C), Brendan Taylor, Wesley Madhevere, Sikandar Raza, Richmond Mutumbami (WK), Tinotenda Mutombodzi, Donald Tiripano, Carl Mumba, Charlton Tshuma.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Liton Das (WK), Tamim Iqbal, Mohammad Naim (ODI DEBUT) (In for Najmul Hossain Shanto), Afif Hossain (ODI DEBUT)(In for Mushfiqur Rahim), Mahmudullah, Mohammad Mithun, Mehidy Hasan, Mashrafe Mortaza (C), Taijul Islam, Mohammad Saifuddin (In for Shafiul Islam), Mustafizur Rahman (In for Al-Amin Hossain).
TOSS - Zimbabwe win the toss and elect to bowl first.

A warm welcome to the final ODI between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe in Sylhet. The hosts would look to make it a whitewash. They would only look to improve their death bowling. Mashrafe Mortaza will be playing his last ODI as captain and it is going to be an emotional moment for him. On the other hand, Zimbabwe can take positives from the last game but would want Brendan Taylor to get a big one. Stay tuned for the teams and the toss.
